title: Isidore Fritz, the great clarinetist who stayed across the lake
summary: Fritz as a self-taught jazz clarinetist who influenced George Lewis and never crossed the lake.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, as I change the subject while I think of it, across the lake I'm wondering about the music there, since most people over here don't know it. Do you remember Isidore Fritz?

Isidore Fritz was one of the greatest clarinetists we had. Jazz kinder. He was nothing but a jazz kinder. He didn't read no music. And he could play anything you play and put harmony to anything you know.
I know George Lewis talks about him being wonderful. I wonder if anybody else ever heard him.
George Lewis got his style from him. George Lewis was coming along.
He really was great you think too?
He was a great player. All the musicians think so, because most everyone went over there and played them there.
He never came over on this side of the lake though I guess.
He never would. He was a brick mace you know.
What kind of a band did he play in do you remember?
